audit.whatIsWrong: The page attributes Ekko's stun to the wrong ability, in five places: whys[5] ("His delayed Phase Dive stun"), spikes[3].text, mid, late and wants.foe[0] all describe a Phase Dive stun. Phase Dive has no stun — Riot's E text is an evasive roll whose next attack deals bonus damage and teleports him to the target, at 325 range with an auto reset. The stun lives on Parallel Convergence: the anomaly arms after a few seconds, slows enemies inside, and stuns only when EKKO himself enters it, which is also where his shield comes from.
audit.why: This is the single most decisive interaction in the matchup and it was pointed at the wrong button. A reader dodging "the Phase Dive stun" is watching the dash while the actual lockdown is a zone already on the ground behind them.
audit.corrected: Stun re-attributed to Parallel Convergence throughout, with the walk-into-it condition stated, and Phase Dive described as what it is — a 325 dash with an auto reset whose tell is the wind-up.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chronobreak's actual behaviour was never stated. The page says it "erases your kill and bursts back" and tells the reader to "burst him down fast", but never that he is untargetable while it casts, never that it heals a percentage of the damage received, never that it returns him to a position he already occupied, and never that the cooldown falls from 110s at rank 1 to 50s at rank 3.
audit.why: Riot's R text gives all four. The untargetability is why dumping your finisher into the cast is the losing play, and the 50s rank-3 cooldown is why "commit on Chronobreak's cooldown" stops being a plan late.
audit.corrected: Untargetability, the rewind-to-a-past-position, the heal and the 110/50 cooldown now carried through winCon, cooldowns, mid, late, spikes[1] and the level chart.
sources: ekko kit R text and cooldown 110/80/50

audit.whatIsWrong: Row 4 contradicts itself across layers: full phases[4].side reads "Ekko" at 7/10 while content win[4] reads "Aurora". The other six full sides read "Skill" against content/packet "Aurora", on a 51% win rate over 1102 games rated TRICKY 7/10.
audit.why: Level 6 is Ekko's, and the kit says why: Chronobreak arrives as an untargetable rewind that refunds the health you spent taking him low. Aurora's level 6 is Between Worlds, which does not answer it. The full layer's Ekko/7-10 verdict is the considered one; win[4] is the stale half.
audit.corrected: win[4] set to Ekko to pair with phases[4].side, with phases[4].why and whys[4] both rewritten in the same proposal. The six "Skill" rows are LEFT ALONE — see notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit, and early told the reader to "punish the long cooldown" on Timewinder — which is 9/8.5/8/7.5/7, the same cooldown as Aurora's own Q.
audit.why: The cooldowns that decide this lane are Chronobreak (110s at rank 1, 50s at rank 3), Parallel Convergence (22s at rank 1) and Phase Dive (9s at 325 range).
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, loading, ahead, late and the phase whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: Range was never mentioned: Timewinder reaches 1075 against Aurora's 900 Q, so the page's premise that Aurora out-pokes him early is unsupported. Meanwhile whys[0] and spikes[0] both call Timewinder easy to dodge "with your dash" — Aurora's E hops backward and is not a dash-through.
audit.why: Riot's Q text: the grenade expands into a time-distortion field on hitting an enemy champion, then rewinds back to Ekko dealing damage on the return. So it must hit a champion to open the field, and it passes twice along the same line.
audit.corrected: Trading text now says he wins the pure poke exchange at 1075, and that stepping off the line beats both passes.
sources: ekko kit Q text and range 1075
aurora kit Q range 900 and E text

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither Grievous Wounds nor Parallel Convergence's shield appeared anywhere in itemization or trading text.
audit.why: The brief flags both: needs-antiheal (Chronobreak's heal) and shield-absorbs-burst (W's shield on entering the anomaly).
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds added to report[8], breakdown.feeding and late; the shield added to breakdown.cooldowns and dontsFull[2].
sources: ekko kit W and R text

audit.whatIsWrong: report[10].t claimed "Your E knockback-slow is clean gank setup" — E has no knockback — and wants.foe[2] said Ekko has "strong global map presence". He has no global ability.
audit.why: Riot's E text for Aurora is damage and slow, then a backward hop. Ekko's map pressure comes from a shoved wave plus Phase Dive and his passive speed burst, not from anything global.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten; the gank note now says a gank that only gets him low is undone by Chronobreak.
sources: ekko kit P and E text

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood pasted, dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad pasted, dosFull[0].d was breakdown.cooldowns pasted, and dosFull[2].d described a whiffed ultimate under the title "Crash waves and ping his roams".
audit.why: Copy-paste bleed — the title promises one thing and the body answers another.
audit.corrected: Each body rewritten against its own title.

edits.before: Phase Dive gives him a delayed stun that's easy to predict once you've seen it once, and your R lets you dodge the follow-up burst entirely if he commits.

edits.before: Ekko's Timewinder has a slow, visible projectile speed, so tracking it and dashing through with E lets you avoid the slow and immediately punish the long cooldown with your own Q. He has no real all-in before 6 outside chip poke, so you control the pace of every early trade as long as you don't eat a lucky Timewinder. Watch his passive charge — three consecutive autos or spells deals bonus damage, so don't stand still through a full trade sequence.
edits.after: Timewinder reaches 1075 against your 900, so he wins the pure poke exchange — but the grenade only expands into its slowing field when it hits a champion, and it comes back through the same line on the way home. Step off that line and the return pass misses too. His entry is Phase Dive, a 325-range roll whose next attack teleports him to you, so the tell is the wind-up, not the cast. Z-Drive Resonance fires on every third hit on the same target — break the sequence and it never lands.

edits.before: At level 6 his Chronobreak becomes a genuine reset threat: taking damage first lets him rewind and heal, so the correct play is to burst him down fast rather than poke slowly into his stun-and-heal combo. If you bait his Phase Dive stun and punish the delay before he can safely rewind, his ultimate becomes a wasted cooldown instead of a comeback tool. He also tends to roam more than fight in lane at this stage, so keep pushing waves to deny his jungle/side-lane impact.
edits.after: At 6 Chronobreak changes what damage is worth. He becomes untargetable as it casts, rewinds to where he stood a few seconds earlier, and heals for a share of what he took in between. So the mistake is not poking too little, it is spending your finisher into the cast. Hold one spell for the landing spot; you can see where he came from. The stun is Parallel Convergence, not Phase Dive: the anomaly arms after a few seconds and only stuns when Ekko walks into it, so refusing to stand on it removes his opener.

edits.before: Your damage race stays ahead of his Z-Drive Resonance proc timing into the late game, and Between Worlds gives you a clean way to dodge his delayed Phase Dive stun if he commits to an all-in. Play around baiting his ultimate cooldown before engaging seriously, since a wasted Chronobreak leaves him with almost no way to punish your poke-and-disengage pattern.
edits.after: Late, Chronobreak is only 50 seconds at rank 3, so you cannot plan around it being down — plan around the landing instead. It returns him to a position he already occupied and damages what is near his arrival, so hold R and your last spell for that spot rather than firing everything into an untargetable cast. Grievous Wounds cuts what the rewind gives back.

notes: BOTH PACKET SUSPECTNAMES ARE FALSE POSITIVES: spikes[1] writes "His Chronobreak" and spikes[2] writes "Z-Drive Resonance" — both are the correct names, the detector just caught the leading word. Those two strings were rewritten anyway, for content reasons unrelated to the names. SIX CHART ROWS LEFT ALONE DELIBERATELY: full phases[0..3,5,6].side read "Skill" while content win[] and the packet chart read "Aurora". I did not flip them — a 51% win rate over 1102 games does not support Aurora owning six of seven rows, and I cannot tell from the kits which layer is right. Only row 4 is resolved, where the two layers openly contradict and Chronobreak grounds the verdict. RATING SEMANTICS: read as the strength of the named side's edge (phases[4] carries "Ekko" at 7/10 while contested rows carry 5-6/10), so no rating needed to move. UNVERIFIED AND NOT WRITTEN: whether Ekko's Parallel Convergence anomaly stuns Aurora while she is invisible inside W, whether Chronobreak's untargetability drops an already-travelling Aurora Q curse or cancels the recast, and whether the anomaly's stun is affected by tenacity. None of that is in Riot's text. ALSO NOT WRITTEN: Chronobreak's arrival damage is described by Riot as "massive" with no number, so I said it damages what is near the landing and left the magnitude out.
